title: The Real Story Behind Victorian Corsets
hook: Tight-lacing deformed ribcages and squished internal organs.

scenes.text: In the 1870s, high Victorian fashion demanded aristocratic women possess an impossibly tiny eighteen-inch 'wasp waist'.

scenes.text: Corsets were reinforced with rigid steel busks and curved whalebone stays, tightened with back cords pulled with all a maid's strength.

scenes.text: Extreme 'tight-lacing' physically compressed the floating ribs inwards, shifting the stomach and liver downwards into unnatural positions.
